project_info.application_name: AWS Connected Vehicle Solution - Vehicle Registration Feature
security_objectives: Protect vehicle registration data stored in DynamoDB and S3
Ensure proper authentication and authorization for API access
Maintain confidentiality and integrity of vehicle registration PDFs
Implement encryption at rest for DynamoDB and S3
Secure API endpoints through Amazon Cognito authentication
Prevent unauthorized access to vehicle data
Protect against injection attacks and data tampering
Implement proper access controls for AWS resources
data_assets: Vehicle registration information (registration number, expiry date)
entry_points: Amazon API Gateway endpoints (ListVehicles, RegisterVehicle, DeregisterVehicle, DescribeVehicle)
trust_boundaries: Between Users and AWS Amplify front-end
Between AWS Amplify and Amazon Cognito (Authentication & Authorization)
Between Amazon Cognito and API Gateway
Between API Gateway and Lambda function
Between Users and S3 (via pre-signed URLs)
project_info.summary: This is a serverless vehicle registration feature for an AWS Connected Vehicle Solution designed for fleet management. The architecture uses AWS Amplify for the front-end, Amazon Cognito for authentication and authorization, API Gateway for API management, Lambda for business logic, DynamoDB for metadata storage, and S3 for PDF document storage. The system provides four main APIs: ListVehicles (returns all available IoT vehicles), RegisterVehicle (registers vehicles with PDF upload), DeregisterVehicle (removes registration and deletes PDFs), and DescribeVehicle (returns vehicle info with pre-signed S3 URLs). Key security features include encryption at rest for both DynamoDB and S3, authentication through Cognito, and the use of pre-signed URLs for secure S3 access. The system assumes a single authorization scope for all APIs and trusts that API Gateway handles authentication before Lambda execution. A critical assumption is that uploaded PDFs are not parsed by custom code, reducing injection attack surface. The architecture follows AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar principles.
